newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 10.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:
* On Monday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended 42.72 points higher at 7,478.50 on the back of a rally in technology and drug stocks.
* On Monday, the Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.51 points, to close at 692.50 points on profit-taking in blue chips Telkom and Sampoerna and some small stocks, brokers said.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,428.90/29.40 at 0150 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.00/29.50.

* Blue chip Bank Negara Indonesia on market talk of a possible merger with another state bank Bank Tabungan Negara. The speculation was revived by reports in a local newspaper on Monday which said the government will merge the seven state banks into four banks.
* Bank Panin after its shareholders approved a plan to issue a 14-for-7 rights issue with three attached warrants at a price of 1,200 rupiah each.
* Consumer finance firm PT Bunas Finance after the company indicated that its first quarter net profit was 135 percent higher compared with the same 1996 period.
* Bank Mashill following reports that Bank Brussels Lambert of Belgium has bought a 10 percent stake from its outstanding shares in the market.
* Confectionery firm Mayora Indah on reports that its planned 300 billion rupiah bond had received an "A "rating from Indonesia's rating agency Pefindo.
* Small paper manufacturer Suparma on reports that it has received shareholder approval to acquire privately-owned PT Siantar Maju at an estimated value of 9.9 billion rupiah.
* Property firm Duta Pertiwi on reports that the firm would issue 350 billion rupiah in bonds. The proceeds would be used to repay debt of its subsidiaries and to finance property projects.
* PT Apac Centertex Corporation, formerly known as Mayatexdian, on a plan to build a pulp plant in Kalimantan with annual production capacity of over 300,000 tonnes.
* Shipping and sea transportation company PT Berlian Laju Tanker on reports that it had secured a $68 million syndicated loan. It will be used to purchase 10 chemical tankers.
* Electronic distribution company PT Telagamas Pertiwi on reports that it had signed an agreeement with PT Naramitra Tara to boost its distribution network.
* Travel and tourism firm Bayu Buana on news that its first quarter net profit was 4.25 billion rupiah, compared with 2.10 billion rupiah in the same 1996 period.

* Herbal cosmetics manufacturer PT Mustika Ratu after it posted a net profit of 19 billion rupiah in 1996, against 16 billion rupiah in 1995. The company also said that it will pay a 1996 dividend of 62 rupiah per share.
